cards.text: Friend, the prophet Isaiah is passing along a message from the LORD to His people, Israel. The LORD calls Himself their Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel. And the first place He brings up is Babylon.

cards.question: The LORD, Israel's Redeemer, says He will send to Babylon. Whose sake does He say He's doing it for?

cards.text: Now, the Chaldeans of Babylon have ships, and they rejoice in those ships. Proud like a guy who just washed his truck and parked it across TWO spaces.

cards.question: The LORD says He will send to Babylon and bring them all as ___, even the Chaldeans, in the ships they rejoice in.

cards.text: Then the LORD says who He is: "I am the LORD, your Holy One, the Creator of Israel, and your King." FOUR titles in one breath, and for years my only title was "What is THIS thing doing in the drawer?"
Then the LORD speaks again. This time He's described as the One who makes a way in the sea and a path through the surging waters.

cards.question: In that picture of the LORD making a way through the sea, what happens to the chariots, horses, armies and warriors He brings out?

answers.text: They lie down never to rise again
They cross the sea behind His people
They turn around and head back home

cards.text: Isaiah says they're extinguished, "snuffed out like a wick". Like the birthday candle I shared that junk drawer with. Used once. Then pfft.

cards.question: Next the LORD tells His people to keep calling the former things to mind.

cards.text: Instead, the LORD says, "Behold, I am about to do something new; even now it is coming. Do you not see it?" That's God going, LOOK UP, it's ON THE WAY!

cards.question: For the new thing that's coming, where does the LORD say He will make a way?

cards.text: And streams in the desert too. The LORD says the wild animals will honor Him for it, the jackals and the ostriches. An ostrich saying thank you? Friend, I would pay GOOD money to see that.

cards.question: The LORD provides water in the wilderness and rivers in the desert. Who does He say it's there to give drink to?
The LORD says the people He formed for Himself will declare His praise.

cards.text: Then the tone flips. After all that talk about rivers in the desert, the LORD turns to Jacob, to Israel, with some hard words.

cards.question: What does the LORD say Jacob, His people Israel, has not done?
The LORD says Israel hasn't called on Him because they have grown ___ of Him.

cards.text: Weary of the One who just promised rivers in the DESERT. Then the LORD gets specific: no sheep for burnt offerings, no honoring Him with sacrifices, no sweet cane bought with their silver.

cards.question: The LORD says He has burdened Israel with offerings and wearied them with frankincense.

cards.text: So nobody's been weighed down by offerings. But somebody HAS been weighed down. And friend, it's not Israel.

cards.question: What does the LORD say Israel has burdened Him with?

cards.text: Sins and iniquities, piled up on the LORD. This is the part where I'd expect God to slam the drawer shut and walk away.

cards.question: Instead, what does the LORD say He does with Israel's transgressions?

cards.text: Listen to how He says it: "I, yes I, am He who blots out your transgressions for My own sake." I, yes I. For My OWN sake. God says "I" twice, like He's making sure nobody in the back row missed who's doing this.

cards.question: The LORD says He will keep remembering Israel's sins.
Then the LORD gives Israel an invitation. What is it?

answers.text: To argue the matter with Him
To bring Him a new offering
To leave the land for good

cards.text: "State your case, so that you may be vindicated." Then the LORD brings up Israel's first father and their spokesmen.

cards.question: The LORD says Israel's first father sinned and their spokesmen rebelled against Him.
So the LORD says He will devote Jacob to ___ and Israel to reproach.

cards.text: And the princes of the sanctuary? Disgraced. That's where this message lands, friend, and it's a heavy place to stop.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 10 quotes "I, yes I, am He who blots out your transgressions for My own sake.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The earlier cards do not give the baker a basis for choosing "weary" rather than "afraid" or "ashamed." All three could explain why someone had stopped calling on God, so this blank guesses at wording the baker has not seen instead of testing a meaning they can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
